rows.quote: For replication analyses, we used COPD GWAS summary statistics from the Million Veteran Program (MVP), which included 103,054 European ancestry cases and 315,450 ancestry-matched controls [26].
rows.coder_note: Step 3 of the decision order (rule C2): the sentence names the Million Veteran Program COPD GWAS (ref 26, Verma 2024), and the outcome side of the dictionary has no Million Veteran Program row under any release; the FinnGen R12 + MVP + UK Biobank meta-analysis is another dataset. No accession, so rule C4 does not apply.

rows.quote: The pQTL data used in this study were obtained from a harmonized dataset compiled by Sun et al. which integrated seven large-scale plasma proteome GWAS (Pietzner, Ferkingstad, Sun, Suhre, Folkersen, Yao, and colleagues) [8–22].
rows.dataset_named_in_source: a harmonized dataset compiled by Sun et al.
rows.coder_note: Step 3 of the decision order (rule C2): the dataset is a harmonized compilation of seven pQTL GWAS by Sun et al. (ref 37 in p002 is Sun J 2023 Genome Med, DOI 10.1186/s13073-023-01229-9, the source of no dictionary row); the pqtl side has no row for this compilation, and the grouped citation [8-22] maps to no single component (rule F). No accession, so rule C4 does not apply.

Step 1 of the decision order (rule H): the sentence in p001 attributes the deCODE data to ref 23 (Eldjarn 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06563-x, which with 'Icelanders' points to the Eldjarn 2023 update row, N 35,892) but gives 35,559 Icelanders as the dataset's N, which is exactly the N of the Ferkingstad 2021 row; two identifiers point to different rows. No accession, so rule C4 does not apply.
